preview: An interview experience for a summer internship at Proctor & Gamble detailing the online assessment, resume screening, presentation, multiple interview rounds, and a final informal chat with the CIO.
content: Interview Experience for Summer Internship. Dishie Vinchhi, Computer 2021-2025. 24th August 2023. We received mail about the on-campus visit of Procter & Gamble. It was visiting VJTI for the first time. Following branches were eligible for the role: B Tech - Computer, IT, Electronics & Telecommunication, Electrical and Electronics Engineering students. There was no eligibility criteria (required CPI) for applying. Online Assessment. 6 pm 25th August 2023 to 6 pm 27th August 2023. The online assessment (total: around 1.5hrs) comprised of two tests: Behavioral questionnaire (No time limit) You can refer to this video to get an idea of the type of questions asked in this section. Some of the questions discussed here may be asked to you in your OA as-it-is. Note: Do not consider the answers marked in the video to be correct. Watch the video to JUST GET AN IDEA OF THE TYPE OF QUESTIONS. Logic and aptitude questionnaire (Timed) In this section, there were different types of questions asked based on mathematics, memory power, logic, etc. 1. Digit challenge. More the number of questions you answer in the given time, higher is the level you attain. 2. Switch challenge. Again, more the number of challenges you solve, higher is the level you attain. 3. Grid challenge - I. Grid Challenge - II. There are a fixed number of challenges in this subsection and hence, no levels. You can practice these types of challenges before your OA to increase your speed in answering. 28th August 2023. 61 students were shortlisted for the next step ie. resume screening on the basis of their performance in the online assessment. We were asked to submit our resumes to the TPO. 30th August 2023. 11 students (4 boys and 7 girls) were shortlisted for the interviews after resume screening. 31st August 2023. Along with the list of 11 students shortlisted, we had received 3 Microsoft Teams links for the interviews which we were told would take place online at 9:20 am on 31st August. At 12:30 am on 31st August, we were informed that the interviews would take place offline at TPO and that we need to reach there before 8:45 am (31st August itself) along with: 2 copies of our resume, Aadhar Card, College ID, Laptop. Tip: Always be prepared for last minute changes in schedule and keep formals, other required documents, etc ready. 1. Presentation. On the day of the interviews, we were seated in the TPO seminar hall and the hiring team introduced themselves and gave a short presentation video on Procter & Gamble at 9:10 am. During the presentation, they asked a few questions to judge our knowledge about the company: What kind of company is P&G? How old is P&G? What is its rank in fortune 500? (Nobody had answered. It is ranked 15 FYI). Tip: You should do some research about the company you are applying for since it creates a good impression if you are aware of the company and its work. They later asked us if we had any questions for them. A few people asked questions about: What kind of work would be expected from interns? What techstack are they looking for? What kind of questions would be asked in interviews? (The lady laughed and said they won’t be giving out their cheatsheet). The session ended at 9:50am. 2. Interview round 1 (35-40 mins). A TPO CR collected our resume copies and submitted them to the panel. We were called in groups of 3 (since there were 3 interviewers) to the cabins in TPO. I was called in the first group itself and asked to go in cabin 6. The interviewer was sitting inside and reading my resume when I entered. Tip : Enter with a smile and do not look scared or panicked and greet him/her. Questions asked: He introduced himself to me and asked me for my introduction. Be prepared with a good introduction of yourself (around 1-1.5 minutes long) since any and every interviewer is going to ask for it. Be sure to include both your technical skills (projects you have worked on, etc) and your hobbies. Later he asked me to explain my GSoC project. I gave a brief overview of it for around 4-5 minutes. He then asked me about why I used the Jax python library in my project and how I managed to go about with it as it was a new library and there were not many online resources to study from. Then, he asked me about a time when I had to make a choice between two options and I was really confused. I talked about the time when I had to choose between IIT Goa and VJTI just after my 12th grade. I continued with how I went about with the evaluation of each and finally came to a conclusion. He seemed happy with my answer and shared a similar situation he had to face. (He had gotten placed in NVIDIA in his final year and at the same time secured admission in IIM-Bangalore. He had finally chosen to pursue an MBA.). Later he asked me a question about my hackathon project. The web application we had made asked users to upload documents and it could answer any questions based on the document. His overall question was whether we can use langchain in a similar manner as used in the project to scan a database and ask questions (like SQL queries but, in simple english) to get responses the way we do in SQL. He asked me to elaborate on how we would go about it. Finally, he asked me if I had any questions for him. Tip: Always ask questions since it shows your interest in getting to know the company better! I told him I had understood the work of an intern at P&G because of the presentation they gave. Since he had mentioned his MBA, I told him about how I was planning to pursue an MBA after some work experience. I asked him what his suggestions would be on the number of years of experience one must have before doing MBA. He told me that if I join a firm like P&G, they would make sure I learn management skills via work and I might not require an MBA! Finally, I thanked him for giving me the opportunity to sit for an interview and how it was nice talking to him. 3. Interview round 2 (35 mins) [3/11 students qualified for round 2]. A few people still had their round 1 going on while I was called for my 2nd round. Out of a total of 3 interviewers, the remaining 2 who hadn’t taken my round 1 interview, together took my 2nd interview. Questions asked: Both introduced themselves and asked me for my introduction. Later, one of them asked me about how my projects were common with another applicant, Labib. I answered by saying that we had one common project as we were on the same team for that hackathon. He asked me about what my contributions were in that project. I explained to him the technical details about the project’s ML backend and how I was a part of the backend team. He asked me about my Eyantra project and what exactly had I worked on in it. I explained for about 3-4 minutes. Then, he asked a question which goes as follows: You have been appointed to solve a problem on the IRCTC website. Many users are trying to access train timings and vacancies simultaneously and everyone is getting a 30 seconds delay in response. The database is found to be giving out responses in 1 second. What could be the possible reasons for this delay? I told him that there might be one user who might have performed a transaction on one of the available tickets and hence, due to cascadeless rollbacks, others were facing a delay. He said this could be a possible reason. He asked for other possibilities. I said there might be a lot of network traffic which the system couldn’t handle. He asked me to elaborate it in terms of computer networking. I told him that I do not have knowledge about CNs as of that time since we had CN in the semester which had just begun and apologized. The second interviewer then started asking Qs. He asked me about a time when I needed help during a project and how I turned to someone else for assistance. I told him about how my GSoC project was based on neuroscience and hence, I found it difficult initially to understand the codebase. I then mentioned that I asked one of my mentors, who was a professor, to teach me basic redundancy and synergy concepts from a neuroscience perspective so that I could understand the codebase a little better. Then, he asked me: If I am on track with a team project which is supposed to be submitted in 2 weeks and suddenly, my boss tells me that we need to submit it in the next 48 hrs, what would my plan of actions be? I proposed 3 ways which I would use in such a situation: Appoint more people with the knowledge in the project’s domain to increase outcome. Motivate the existing team members to work for extra hours since they have been putting efforts since a long time and everyone should get fruitful results of the same. Try to understand the reason for the preponement of the deadline. If it is because they want a particular part of the project, in 48 hrs, we could implement and submit that specific subtask. Both of them asked me if I had questions for them. Again, always show interest in the company, interviewer’s career path by asking questions. 4. Not-an-interview round 3 (10 mins). I was called at 12:35 again for an online meeting with the CIO of P&G. A lady (not an interviewer but more of a communication-with-TPO person) from the panel asked me to “chill” before I went into the cabin. She gave me an introduction of the CIO and how this would not be an interview. She said the CIO just wants to talk to me for 5 minutes to know me well. I felt quite relaxed after listening to what she said! The meet was on Microsoft Teams and it lasted for 10 mins. It was a very informal chat with the CIO. He introduced himself and spoke about how P&G is different from other corporate companies and how they are a “people-company” and care about all employees. I then introduced myself. He asked me about how my interviews went that day and if I had any questions for him. 5. Results. The results were announced on the same day at around 1:45 pm. Two people (1 boy, 1 girl) were offered an internship. 6. Other Tips: I wasn’t asked puzzles however, a few interviewees were asked questions like: 3 ants in a triangle, Find the only heavy ball from N balls by performing minimum no. of comparisons. Stay confident and composed while answering questions. P&G mainly focuses on the personality and thinking process of students during interviews since the technical skills are pretty much visible on their CVs. (And hence, a strong resume is a must). They want to see how adaptable the student is to situations which usually cause panic.
